population_label: replicates in which the same seeded lookup sample was replayed against both index designs
not_shown: Server-side `took` only: Elasticsearch's own reported execution time, excluding HTTP transport and client overhead. It is the honest measure of what the mapping change bought and must never be read as what a caller experiences -- the wall-clock figure beside it is that. The published value is the WEAKEST of the replicates, not a central tendency; the raw runs travel in `runs`.

population_label: replicates in which the same seeded lookup sample was replayed against both index designs
not_shown: Client-side wall time, including HTTP transport and Python-client overhead. It carries a roughly constant floor the index design cannot touch, which dilutes the ratio -- so it is SMALLER than the server-side figure by construction and is reported because quoting only the flattering clock would be the whole problem. The published value is the WEAKEST of the replicates; the raw runs travel in `runs`.

population_label: per-arm records that replayed the seeded sample and agreed on its size
not_shown: The MEASURED sample only. Each arm also runs an uncounted 50-lookup warmup first, so neither side pays a cold-cache penalty the other avoids; those warmup lookups are not in this count and are not in any latency distribution.

population_label: replicates whose two indices were independently counted after the force-merge and agreed
not_shown: Documents in EACH index, not across both. Both are generated from one seed, so the two corpora are identical and the loader refuses outright if the live counts differ.

population_label: replicates that agreed on this total, which the fixed seed and fixed lookup order make deterministic
not_shown: Summed over the whole replayed sample, not per lookup. The two designs are NOT expected to return identical hit sets: analyzed text fields tokenize dimension values, so the dynamic-mapping design is genuinely fuzzier and matches a superset. That is what makes it the wrong tool, not an artifact of the benchmark.

population_label: replicates that agreed on this total, which the fixed seed and fixed lookup order make deterministic
not_shown: The exact design's total. It is SMALLER than the naive design's by design, and the guard that makes the latency comparison meaningful is one-sided: the fuzzy design must match at least as many, or a faster arm would simply be a smaller query.

population_label: arm replays examined for lookups that matched nothing (both arms of every replicate)
not_shown: A count of occurrences over a stated denominator, never a rate. A zero here is a MEASURED zero: the denominator beside it says how many lookups were examined to find it, which is what separates it from a check that examined nothing. This is the condition that failed at smoke corpus size, where 11 lookups across the two arms matched nothing.
